skill.name: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) Policy Learning
skill.description: A simplified offline algorithm for fine-tuning language models directly from preference data without requiring an explicit reward model. Uses log-ratio of policy and reference model likelihoods to formulate implicit rewards.
skill.skill_body:
Apply DPO to fine-tune a policy model from preference pairs. Reparameterize the reward function using the log ratio of likelihood between the current policy model and a supervised fine-tuned (SFT) reference model. Train the policy to maximize the implicit reward derived from this formulation, eliminating the need for a separate reward model training stage.

## Objective

Align language models with human preferences through direct policy optimization without explicit reward model training
## Applicable Signals

- Preference pairs available from human feedback or comparative evaluations
- Need to fine-tune LLM without training a separate reward model
- Seeking simpler, more stable alternative to multi-stage RLHF
- Offline learning scenario with fixed preference dataset

## Contraindications

- Do not use if explicit reward model is already trained and validated
- Do not use if online RL feedback collection is feasible and preferred
- Do not use if reward function must be independently interpretable for compliance or auditing
- Do not use if preference data is sparse or unreliable

## Intervention Moves

- Prepare preference dataset with chosen and rejected response pairs
- Initialize policy model from supervised fine-tuned (SFT) baseline
- Compute log-ratio of policy and reference model likelihoods for each pair using Reward Formulation via Policy-Reference Log Ratio micro-skill
- Formulate implicit reward using the log-ratio parameterization
- Optimize policy to maximize preference-aligned implicit reward
- Evaluate on held-out preference test set

## Constraints

- Requires a reference SFT model as baseline for likelihood computation
- Requires preference pairs (chosen vs. rejected responses) as training data
- Implicit reward formulation is tied to log-ratio; cannot be extracted or inspected independently
- Offline setting: no online interaction or iterative feedback collection

## Cautions

- Implicit reward may not align with explicit human values if preference data is biased
- Log-ratio formulation assumes reference model is a reasonable baseline; poor SFT initialization may degrade results
- Preference pairs must be comparable (same prompt, different responses) for meaningful optimization

## Output Contract

- Fine-tuned policy model that ranks preferred responses higher than dispreferred ones on held-out preference test set. Model should demonstrate improved alignment with human preferences compared to the SFT baseline.
